name: gaffer
description: Reusable orchestration layer for Claude Code: a chief-engineer/architect/ux-designer/reviewer/implementer subagent team, a new-project bootstrap chain (stack-agnostic, spec-driven via a VERSION-PINNED gspec read through a single adapter, with plugin-owned cross-feature sequencing in .agents/roadmap.yaml), and a review chain, graduated autonomy across four levels (interactive → supervised → autonomous → full-autonomy, set in-session via /gaffer:set-autonomy, Desktop-friendly) where full-autonomy delegates merge/rebase/push onto non-main branches while keeping main, releases, and the danger floor human-gated — with a pausable/resumable, crash-safe guided loop (durable run-state checkpoints that auto-resume on reopen, with write-ahead recovery) that picks its own execution mode from the backlog size — running inline for small runs, or relaying one freshly-dispatched chief-engineer per packet once the backlog passes the measured ~20-packet crossover, where relaying is both cheaper and the only mode that finishes a long run without exhausting the session window (overridable with --relay/--inline), a single-checkout feature-branch workflow (develop integration branch + orch/* packet branches, no worktrees), a task-packet template (with per-packet TDD method + consumes/produces interface contract), and a three-tier approval guardrail hook (read-only fast-path allows searches/inspection immediately; a one-click ask tier for routine-but-notable actions like dependency installs, migrations, and deploys; hard-deny for the irreversible surface — auth/secrets writes, git history destruction, recursive deletes) covering the risks common to any codebase, with domain-specific risk (e.g. money movement) declared per-repo via .agents/guard-extra-paths rather than baked in.
